headline: High: Opik’s broad network egress can exfiltrate data if paired with a shared workspace or trusted handoff from awesome-selfhosted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-selfhosted and opik. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while opik only exposes a REST API and broad egress. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies awesome-selfhosted content into opik prompts or API payloads, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not pipe outputs between them.
Disable any copy-paste or clipboard automation between tools.
Use a provenance tag on any imported text before sending it to opik.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a read-only knowledge-management artifact with no touched data classes, while opik has broad network egress and REST API access. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data by default, so leakage is only plausible if the operator routes local files or secrets into opik.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files in a shared workspace and opik reads them, leakage risk increases.
IF opik is configured to send request payloads containing local content to its backend, data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Do not store secrets in any shared folder used by opik.
Review opik API payloads before sending.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for awesome-selfhosted references.
Turn off any automatic file ingestion into opik.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface or mutable shared resource in the profiles. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and exposes no write capability, while opik only advertises REST API calls and broad egress, not filesystem or git writes. The conflict pathway is therefore not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared mutable state, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep write permissions absent for both agents.
Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both tools.
If shared state is needed, add explicit locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can supply curated references, and opik can consume API inputs, but neither profile shows autonomous action-taking or a default trust chain. The cascade exists only if the operator treats awesome-selfhosted content as authoritative input to opik without verification, so the blast radius is limited and conditional.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted content is copied into opik as ground truth without review, errors can cascade.
IF opik is used to generate downstream reports or actions from that copied content, impact grows.
mitigations: Verify any imported reference before using it in opik.
Require a human review step between the two tools.
Label imported content as untrusted in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency constraint, or retention policy is documented for either agent. awesome-selfhosted is a static open-source knowledge-management project, and opik’s profile does not show PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data handling. With only docs-level evidence, no specific compliance mismatch is established.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, a separate compliance review is required.
IF opik is configured to store or transmit regulated content, residency and retention must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid using regulated data in this pair.
Review retention settings if opik stores outputs.
